subject: CC
stem: Which method is considered the reference method for glucose determination?
explanation: The hexokinase method is the reference method because it is highly specific and less affected by interferences than glucose oxidase. Folin-Wu and o-toluidine are older, less specific methods. Reference: StatPearls, Hexokinase Method (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK587446).

subject: CC
stem: Which enzyme is the most specific marker for acute pancreatitis?
explanation: Lipase is more specific to the pancreas than amylase and stays elevated longer after an attack of acute pancreatitis. Reference: StatPearls, Biochemistry, Lipase (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537346).

subject: CC
stem: Which lipoprotein carries most of the cholesterol to peripheral tissues?
explanation: LDL delivers cholesterol to peripheral cells (the 'bad' cholesterol). HDL does reverse cholesterol transport back to the liver. Reference: StatPearls, Biochemistry, Cholesterol (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK513326).

subject: CC
stem: Which formula correctly computes the anion gap (without potassium)?
explanation: Anion gap = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻). When potassium is included it becomes (Na⁺ + K⁺) − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻). Reference: StatPearls, Biochemistry, Anion Gap (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK539757).

subject: CC
stem: The Jaffe reaction for creatinine uses which reagent?
explanation: In the Jaffe reaction, creatinine reacts with alkaline picrate to form a red-orange complex. Diacetyl monoxime is for urea, phosphotungstic acid for uric acid, and o-cresolphthalein for calcium. Reference: Peake & Whiting, Measurement of Serum Creatinine, Clin Biochem Rev 2006 (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1784008).

subject: CC
stem: What is the best initial screening test for suspected primary thyroid dysfunction?
explanation: TSH is the most sensitive indicator of thyroid dysfunction, so it is the first-line screening test; free T4 is added when TSH is abnormal. Reference: StatPearls, Physiology, Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499850).

subject: CC
stem: In healthy adults, serum cortisol is normally highest:
choices: In the early morning, soon after waking
explanation: Cortisol follows a 24-hour (circadian) rhythm: it peaks in the early morning after waking and is lowest around midnight, so the collection time matters. Reference: Development of 24-Hour Rhythms in Cortisol Secretion, meta-analysis (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11747683).

subject: CC
stem: In Westgard multirule quality control, the 1-3s rule is violated when:
choices: Two consecutive controls exceed the same ±2SD limit
One control result falls outside the mean ±3SD
One control exceeds +2SD and another exceeds −2SD in the same run
Ten consecutive results fall on one side of the mean
explanation: 1-3s = a single control beyond ±3SD. It is a rejection rule and usually points to random error. 2-2s detects systematic error, R-4s random error within a run, and 10x a shift. Reference: Westgard QC, Westgard Rules (westgard.com/westgard-rules.html).

subject: CC
stem: According to Beer's law, the absorbance of a solution is:
choices: Directly proportional to its concentration and the light path length
Independent of the light path length
explanation: A = εbc: absorbance rises linearly with concentration and path length, so a plot of absorbance against concentration is a straight line through zero (it bends at high concentrations). Reference: Chemistry LibreTexts, Beer-Lambert Law (chem.libretexts.org, Organic Chemistry Glossary).

subject: CC
stem: An AST:ALT ratio of 2:1 or higher most suggests:
explanation: AST rises more than ALT in alcohol-related liver disease, so an AST:ALT ratio of 2:1 or more points to it. Reference: StatPearls, Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK562172) and Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK546632).

subject: CC
stem: Which enzyme rises most markedly in biliary (obstructive) liver disease?
explanation: A marked rise in alkaline phosphatase, with normal or only mildly raised transaminases, points to biliary obstruction. Reference: StatPearls, Hyperbilirubinemia (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK544252).

subject: CC
stem: The most abundant protein in human plasma is:
explanation: Albumin makes up about half of total plasma protein (3.5–5 g/dL) and most of the plasma oncotic pressure. Reference: StatPearls, Physiology, Albumin (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459198).

subject: CC
stem: The biuret method for total protein is based on:
choices: Aromatic amino acids absorbing light at 280 nm
Peptide bonds forming a violet complex with Cu²⁺ in alkaline solution
Free amino groups reacting with ninhydrin
explanation: In alkaline solution, cupric ions bind the nitrogens of peptide bonds and turn violet; free amino acids do not react. It is simple but relatively insensitive. Reference: Biology LibreTexts, Fundamentals of Biochemistry, 3.3 Proteins: Analyses and Structural Predictions (bio.libretexts.org).

subject: CC
stem: In therapeutic drug monitoring, a trough level is collected:
choices: At the time of peak absorption
Exactly 1 hour after an IV dose
explanation: The trough is the lowest concentration, reached just before the next dose; the peak reflects maximum absorption. Reference: Overview of Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2687654).

subject: CC
stem: Carbon monoxide is toxic mainly because it:
choices: Oxidizes heme iron to the ferric state
Binds hemoglobin about 200–250 times more strongly than oxygen
explanation: CO forms carboxyhemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen. Oxidized (ferric) heme iron is methemoglobin, and acetylcholinesterase inhibition is the mechanism of organophosphates. Reference: StatPearls, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557888).
